chunks: Is'haq, from Abū Hāshim al-Ja‘farī, who said:

I entered upon Abū Muḥammad one day, while I intended to ask him what I should fashion a ring from so that I might seek blessing through it. So I sat down, and I was made to forget what I had come to him for.

Then when I bade farewell and rose, he threw the ring toward me and said: 'You wanted silver, so We gave you a ring. You gained the stone and the crafting cost as well. May Allah bless you with joy, O Abū Hāshim.'
So I said: 'O my master, I bear witness that you are the Walī of Allah and my Imam, through obedience to whom I practice my religion before Allah.' He said: 'May Allah forgive you, O Abū Hāshim.'

key_terms.أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ: Abū Muḥammad, the kunyah of Imam al-Ḥasan al-‘Askarī عليه السلام
key_terms.إِمَامِيَ: my Imam, the one acknowledged as rightful religious guide
key_terms.بِطَاعَتِهِ: through obeying him, indicating religious allegiance
key_terms.خَاتَمًا: a ring given as a blessed object
key_terms.فِضَّةً: silver, the material Abū Hāshim intended for the ring
key_terms.وَلِيُّ اللَّهِ: the guardian and intimate authority of Allah

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show the knowledge and spiritual authority of Imam al-Ḥasan al-‘Askarī عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This narration recounts an encounter with Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام in which he knew Abū Hāshim’s unspoken intention and fulfilled it before being asked. The report highlights the Imam’s spiritual knowledge, the blessing associated with him, and Abū Hāshim’s affirmation of his wilayah and Imamate.
